[Gu04] Guy, Richard K., Unsolved problems in number theory. (2004), xviii+437.
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ ε,
  (ε =o[Filter.atTop] fun x => 1) ∧
    ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ↑(Erdos241.f N 3) ≤ ((7 / 2) ^ (1 / 3) + ε N) * ↑N ^ (1 / 3)

declarations.docstring:
For every $n>2$ there exist distinct integers $1 ≤ x < y < z$
such that $\frac 4 n = \frac 1 x + \frac 1 y + \frac 1 z$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/242](https://www.erdosproblems.com/242)
[Si56](https://zbmath.org/?q=an%3A0075.03302) Sierpiński, W., Sur les décompositions de nombres rationnels en fractions primaires. Mathesis (1956), 16--32.

declarations.docstring:
Schinzel conjectured (see [Si56]) the generalisation that, for any fixed $a$, if $n$ is sufficiently
large in terms of $a$ then there exist distinct integers $1\leq x < y < z$ such that
$\frac{a}{n} = \frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{y}+\frac{1}{z}.$
references: [erdosproblems.com/242](https://www.erdosproblems.com/242)
[Si56](https://zbmath.org/?q=an%3A0075.03302) Sierpiński, W., Sur les décompositions de nombres rationnels en fractions primaires. Mathesis (1956), 16--32.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (a : ℕ), 0 < a → ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ x y z, 1 ≤ x ∧ x < y ∧ y < z ∧ ↑a / ↑n = 1 / ↑x + 1 / ↑y + 1 / ↑z

declarations.docstring:
Let $a_1 < a_2 < \dots$ be a sequence of integers such that
$\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{a_n}{a_{n-1}^2} = 1$ and $\sum \frac{1}{a_n} \in \mathbb{Q}$.

Then, for all sufficiently large $n \ge 1$, $a_n = a_{n-1}^2 - a_{n-1} + 1$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/243](https://www.erdosproblems.com/243)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ),
  StrictMono a →
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(a n) / ↑(a (n - 1)) ^ 2) Filter.atTop (nhds 1) →
      (Summable fun x => 1 / ↑(a x)) → ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, a n = a (n - 1) ^ 2 - a (n - 1) + 1

declarations.docstring:
Let $C > 1$. Does the set of integers of the form $p + \lfloor C^k \rfloor$,
for some prime $p$ and $k\geq 0$, have density $>0$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/244](https://www.erdosproblems.com/244)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ C > 1, 0 < {x | ∃ p k, ∃ (_ : Nat.Prime p), p + ⌊C ^ k⌋₊ = x}.lowerDensity

declarations.docstring:
Romanoff [Ro34] proved that the answer is yes if $C$ is an integer.

[Ro34] Romanoff, N. P., _Über einige Sätze der additiven Zahlentheorie_.
Math. Ann. (1934), 668-678.
references: [erdosproblems.com/244](https://www.erdosproblems.com/244)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {C : ℕ}, 1 < C → 0 < {x | ∃ p k, ∃ (_ : Nat.Prime p), p + ⌊C ^ k⌋₊ = x}.lowerDensity

declarations.docstring:
Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set such that $|A\cap \{1, ..., N\}| = o(N)$.
Is it true that
$$
\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac{|(A + A)\cap \{1, ..., N\}|}{|A \cap \{1, ..., N\}|} \geq 3?
$$

The answer is yes, proved by Freiman [Fr73].

[Fr73] Fre\u{\i}man, G. A., _Foundations of a structural theory of set addition_. (1973), vii+108.
references: [erdosproblems.com/245](https://www.erdosproblems.com/245)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (A : Set ℕ),
    A.Infinite →
      Filter.Tendsto (fun N => ↑(A ∩ Set.Icc 1 ⌊N⌋₊).ncard / N) Filter.atTop (nhds 0) →
        3 ≤ Filter.limsup (fun N => ↑((A + A) ∩ Set.Icc 1 ⌊N⌋₊).ncard / ↑(A ∩ Set.Icc 1 ⌊N⌋₊).ncard) Filter.atTop

declarations.docstring:
Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set such that $|A\cap \{1, ..., N\}| = o(N)$.
Then
$$
\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac{|(A + A)\cap \{1, ..., N\}|}{|A \cap \{1, ..., N\}|} \geq 2.
$$
references: [erdosproblems.com/245](https://www.erdosproblems.com/245)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (A : Set ℕ),
  A.Infinite →
    Filter.Tendsto (fun N => ↑(A ∩ Set.Icc 1 ⌊N⌋₊).ncard / N) Filter.atTop (nhds 0) →
      2 ≤ Filter.limsup (fun N => ↑((A + A) ∩ Set.Icc 1 ⌊N⌋₊).ncard / ↑(A ∩ Set.Icc 1 ⌊N⌋₊).ncard) Filter.atTop

declarations.docstring:
Let $(a,b)=1$. The set $\{a^kb^l: k,l\geq 0\}$ is complete - that is, every large integer is the sum of distinct integers of the form $a^kb^l$ with $k,l\geq 0$.

We state the nontrivial case $a,b\geq 2$, proved by Birch [Bi59].
references: [erdosproblems.com/246](https://www.erdosproblems.com/246)
[Bi59] Birch, B. J., *Note on a problem of Erd\H{o}s*. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. (1959), 370-373.
[Ca60] Cassels, J. W. S., *On the representation of integers as the sums of distinct summands taken from a fixed set*. Acta Sci. Math. (Szeged) (1960), 111-124.
[FaCh17] Fang, Jin-Hui and Chen, Yong-Gao, *A quantitative form of the {E}rd\H{o}s-{B}irch theorem*. Acta Arith. (2017), 301--311.
[He00b] Hegyv\'{a}ri, N., *On the completeness of an exponential type sequence*. Acta Math. Hungar. (2000), 127--135.
[Yu24] Yu, Wang-Xing, *On the representation of an exponential type sequence*. Publ. Math. Debrecen (2024), 253--261.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (a b : ℕ), 2 ≤ a → 2 ≤ b → a.Coprime b → IsAddComplete (Erdos246.Gamma a b)

declarations.docstring:
Let $n_1 < n_2 < \cdots$ be a sequence of integers such that
$$
  \limsup \frac{n_k}{k} = \infty.
$$
Is
$$
  \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{2^{n_k}}
$$
transcendental?
references: [erdosproblems.com/247](https://www.erdosproblems.com/247)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (n : ℕ → ℕ),
    StrictMono n →
      Filter.limsup (fun k => ↑(n k) / ↑k.succ) Filter.atTop = ⊤ → Transcendental ℚ (∑' (k : ℕ), 1 / 2 ^ n k)

declarations.docstring:
Erdős proved the answer is yes under the stronger condition that
$\limsup \frac{n_k}{k^t} = \infty$ for all $t\geq 1$.

[ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R.,
_Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory_.
Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
references: [erdosproblems.com/247](https://www.erdosproblems.com/247)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (n : ℕ → ℕ),
  StrictMono n →
    (∀ t ≥ 1, Filter.limsup (fun k => ↑(↑(n k) / ↑k.succ ^ t)) Filter.atTop = ⊤) →
      Transcendental ℚ (∑' (k : ℕ), 1 / 2 ^ n k)

declarations.docstring:
Are there infinitely many $n$ such that $\omega(n + k) \ll k$ for all $k \geq 1$?
Here $\omega(n)$ is the number of distinct prime divisors of $n$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/248](https://www.erdosproblems.com/248)
[TaTe25] T. Tao and J. Teräväinen, Quantitative correlations and some problems on prime factors of consecutive integers. arXiv:2512.01739 (2025).

declarations.docstring:
Is
$$\sum_{n} \frac{\phi(n)}{2^n}$$
irrational? Here $\phi$ is the Euler totient function.
references: [erdosproblems.com/249](https://www.erdosproblems.com/249)

declarations.docstring:
Let $n_1 < n_2 < \dots$ be an arbitrary sequence of integers, each with an associated residue class
$a_i \pmod{n_i}$. Let $A$ be the set of integers $n$ such that for every $i$ either $n < n_i$ or
$n \not\equiv a_i \pmod{n_i}$. Must the logarithmic density of $A$ exist?
references: [erdosproblems.com/25](https://www.erdosproblems.com/25)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (seq_n : ℕ → ℕ) (seq_a : ℕ → ℤ),
    (∀ (i : ℕ), 0 < seq_n i) →
      StrictMono seq_n → ∃ d, {x | ∀ (i : ℕ), ↑x < ↑(seq_n i) ∨ ¬↑x ≡ seq_a i [ZMOD ↑(seq_n i)]}.HasLogDensity d

declarations.docstring:
Is
$$
  \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{\sigma(n)}{2^n}
$$
irrational? Here $\sigma(n)$ is the sum of divisors function.

The answer is yes, as shown by Nesterenko [Ne96].

[Ne96] Nesterenko, Yu V., _Modular functions and transcendence questions_,
Mat. Sb. 187 *9* (1996), 1319--1348.
references: [erdosproblems.com/250](https://www.erdosproblems.com/250)
declarations.type_pretty: (∀ (x : ℝ), HasSum (fun n => ↑((ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1) n) / 2 ^ n) x → Irrational x) ↔ True

declarations.docstring: Is $\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{p_n}{2^n}$ irrational? Here $p_n$ is the $n$-th prime ($p_1=2, p_2=3, \dots$).
references: [erdosproblems.com/251](https://www.erdosproblems.com/251)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ Irrational (∑' (n : ℕ), ↑(Nat.nth Nat.Prime n) / 2 ^ n)

$\frac{a_{i+1}}{a_i} \to 1$. If every arithmetic progression contains infinitely many
integers which are the sum of distinct $a_i$ then every sufficiently large integer is

declarations.type_pretty:
¬∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ),
    0 < a 0 →
      Erdos253.RepresentsAPs a →
        Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(a (n + 1)) / ↑(a n)) Filter.atTop (nhds 1) →
          subsetSums (Set.range a) ∈ Filter.cofinite

declarations.docstring:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be such that $\lvert A\cap [1,2x]\rvert -\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert \to
\infty\textrm{ as }x\to \infty$ and $\sum_{n\in A} \{ \theta n\}=\infty$ for every $\theta\in
(0,1)$, where $\{x\}$ is the distance of $x$ from the nearest integer. Then every sufficiently large
integer is the sum of distinct elements of $A$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/254](https://www.erdosproblems.com/254)
[Ca60] Cassels, J. W. S., On the representation of integers as the sums of distinct summands taken from a fixed set. Acta Sci. Math. (Szeged) (1960), 111-124.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (A : Set ℕ),
  (Filter.Tendsto (fun x => (A ∩ Set.Icc 1 (2 * x)).ncard - (A ∩ Set.Icc 1 x).ncard) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop ∧
      ∀ (θ : ℝ), 0 < θ → θ < 1 → ¬Summable fun n => distToNearestInt (θ * ↑↑n)) →
    ∀ᶠ (m : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, Erdos254.IsSumOfDistinct A m

declarations.docstring:
Cassels [Ca60] proved this under the alternative hypotheses $\lim \frac{\lvert A\cap [1,2x]\rvert
-\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert}{\log\log x}=\infty$ and $\sum_{n\in A} \{ \theta n\}^2=\infty$ for every
$\theta\in (0,1)$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/254](https://www.erdosproblems.com/254)
[Ca60] Cassels, J. W. S., On the representation of integers as the sums of distinct summands taken from a fixed set. Acta Sci. Math. (Szeged) (1960), 111-124.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (A : Set ℕ),
  (Filter.Tendsto (fun x => (↑(A ∩ Set.Icc 1 (2 * x)).ncard - ↑(A ∩ Set.Icc 1 x).ncard) / Real.log (Real.log ↑x))
        Filter.atTop Filter.atTop ∧
      ∀ (θ : ℝ), 0 < θ → θ < 1 → ¬Summable fun n => distToNearestInt (θ * ↑↑n) ^ 2) →
    ∀ᶠ (m : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, Erdos254.IsSumOfDistinct A m

declarations.docstring:
The hypothesis `¬ Summable (fun n : A ↦ distToNearestInt (θ * n))` used below says exactly
that the partial sums of `‖θ n‖` over `n ∈ A` diverge, which is the form the linked proof uses.
`distToNearestInt` is nonnegative, so this is an instance of
`not_summable_subtype_iff_tendsto_sum_indicator`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/254](https://www.erdosproblems.com/254)
[Ca60] Cassels, J. W. S., On the representation of integers as the sums of distinct summands taken from a fixed set. Acta Sci. Math. (Szeged) (1960), 111-124.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (A : Set ℕ) (θ : ℝ),
  (¬Summable fun n => distToNearestInt (θ * ↑↑n)) ↔
    Filter.Tendsto (fun N => ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, A.indicator (fun n => distToNearestInt (θ * ↑n)) n) Filter.atTop
      Filter.atTop

declarations.docstring:
Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set. Is
$$
\sum_{n\in A} \frac{1}{2^n - 1}
$$
irrational?
references: [erdosproblems.com/257](https://www.erdosproblems.com/257)

declarations.docstring:
Show that
$$
\sum_{n} \frac{d(n)}{2^n}
$$
is irrational.

[Er48] Erdős, P., _On arithmetical properties of Lambert series_. J. Indian Math. Soc. (N.S.) (1948), 63-66.
references: [erdosproblems.com/257](https://www.erdosproblems.com/257)

declarations.docstring:
Show that
$$
\sum_{n} \frac{1}{2^n - 1} = \sum_{n} \frac{d(n)}{2^n},
$$
where $d(n)$ is the number of divisors of $n$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/257](https://www.erdosproblems.com/257)

declarations.docstring:
Let $a_n \to \infty$ be a sequence of non-zero natural numbers. Is
$\sum_n \frac{d(n)}{(a_1 ... a_n)}$ irrational, where $d(n)$ is the number of divisors of $n$?

This was proved affirmatively by Chojecki and GPT-5.4 Pro [Ch26], and formalised in Lean
by ster-oc [St26].
references: [erdosproblems.com/258](https://www.erdosproblems.com/258)
[Ch26] P. Chojecki and GPT-5.4 Pro, [Erdős problem 258](https://www.ulam.ai/research/erdos258.pdf) (2026)

[St26] ster-oc, [Lean formalisation of Erdős problem 258](https://live.lean-lang.org/#project=mathlib-v4.28.0&url=https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ster-oc/2b7adcf9d753cf6e29d782f7374cc57e/raw/689a8483895cbe147634dfbf2d7b1db93a3b5b5f/Erdos258.lean) (2026)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ),
    (∀ (n : ℕ), 2 ≤ a n) →
      Filter.Tendsto a Filter.atTop Filter.atTop →
        Irrational (∑' (n : ℕ), ↑(n + 1).divisors.card / ↑(∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (n + 1), a i))

declarations.docstring:
Is $\sum_n \frac{d(n)}{t^n}$ irrational, where $t ≥ 2$ is an integer.

Solution: True (proved by Erdős, see Erdős Problems website)
references: [erdosproblems.com/258](https://www.erdosproblems.com/258)
[Ch26] P. Chojecki and GPT-5.4 Pro, [Erdős problem 258](https://www.ulam.ai/research/erdos258.pdf) (2026)

[St26] ster-oc, [Lean formalisation of Erdős problem 258](https://live.lean-lang.org/#project=mathlib-v4.28.0&url=https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ster-oc/2b7adcf9d753cf6e29d782f7374cc57e/raw/689a8483895cbe147634dfbf2d7b1db93a3b5b5f/Erdos258.lean) (2026)

declarations.docstring:
Let $2 \leq a_1 \leq a_2 \leq \cdots$ be a monotone sequence with $a_n \to \infty$.
Is $\sum_n \frac{d(n)}{a_1 \cdots a_n}$ irrational, where $d(n)$ is the number of divisors of $n$?

Solution: True (proved by Erdős and Straus [ErSt71], Lemma 2.2 and Theorem 2.13).
references: [erdosproblems.com/258](https://www.erdosproblems.com/258)
[Ch26] P. Chojecki and GPT-5.4 Pro, [Erdős problem 258](https://www.ulam.ai/research/erdos258.pdf) (2026)

[St26] ster-oc, [Lean formalisation of Erdős problem 258](https://live.lean-lang.org/#project=mathlib-v4.28.0&url=https://gist.githubusercontent.com/ster-oc/2b7adcf9d753cf6e29d782f7374cc57e/raw/689a8483895cbe147634dfbf2d7b1db93a3b5b5f/Erdos258.lean) (2026)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ),
    (∀ (n : ℕ), 2 ≤ a n) →
      Monotone a →
        Filter.Tendsto a Filter.atTop Filter.atTop →
          Irrational (∑' (n : ℕ), ↑(n + 1).divisors.card / ↑(∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (n + 1), a i))

declarations.docstring:
Is $\sum_{n} \mu(n)^2\frac{n}{2^n}$ irrational?

This is true, and was proved by Chen and Ruzsa.

[ChRu99] Chen, Yong-Gao and Ruzsa, Imre Z., On the irrationality of certain series. Period. Math. Hungar. (1999), 31--37.
references: [erdosproblems.com/259](https://www.erdosproblems.com/259)

declarations.docstring:
Let $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ be infinite such that $\sum_{a \in A} \frac{1}{a} = \infty$. Must
there exist some $k\geq 1$ such that almost all integers have a divisor of the form $a+k$
for some $a\in A$?

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev using Aristotle.
references: [erdosproblems.com/26](https://www.erdosproblems.com/26)
[Te19](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1908.00488) G. Tenenbaum, _Some of Erdős' unconventional problems in number theory, thirty-four years later_, arXiv:1908.00488 [math.NT] (2019)
declarations.type_pretty: False ↔ ∀ (A : ℕ → ℕ), StrictMono A → Erdos26.IsThick A → ∃ k, Erdos26.IsBehrend fun x => A x + k

declarations.docstring: If we allow for $\sum_{a\in A} \frac{1}{a} < \infty$ then Rusza has found a counter-example.
references: [erdosproblems.com/26](https://www.erdosproblems.com/26)
[Te19](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1908.00488) G. Tenenbaum, _Some of Erdős' unconventional problems in number theory, thirty-four years later_, arXiv:1908.00488 [math.NT] (2019)
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ A, StrictMono A ∧ ¬Erdos26.IsThick A ∧ ∀ (k : ℕ), ¬Erdos26.IsBehrend fun x => A x + k

declarations.docstring:
Tenenbaum asked the weaker variant where for every $\epsilon>0$ there is
some $k=k(\epsilon)$ such that at least $1-\epsilon$ density of all integers have a
divisor of the form $a+k$ for some $a\in A$.

The DeepMind prover agent has found a formal disproof of this statement.
references: [erdosproblems.com/26](https://www.erdosproblems.com/26)
[Te19](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1908.00488) G. Tenenbaum, _Some of Erdős' unconventional problems in number theory, thirty-four years later_, arXiv:1908.00488 [math.NT] (2019)
declarations.type_pretty: False ↔ ∀ (A : ℕ → ℕ), StrictMono A → Erdos26.IsThick A → ∀ ε > 0, ∃ k, Erdos26.IsWeaklyBehrend (fun x => A x + k) ε

references: [erdosproblems.com/26](https://www.erdosproblems.com/26)
[Te19](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1908.00488) G. Tenenbaum, _Some of Erdős' unconventional problems in number theory, thirty-four years later_, arXiv:1908.00488 [math.NT] (2019)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {ι : Type u_1} (A : ι → ℕ), 1 ∈ Set.range A → Erdos26.IsBehrend A

references: [erdosproblems.com/26](https://www.erdosproblems.com/26)
[Te19](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1908.00488) G. Tenenbaum, _Some of Erdős' unconventional problems in number theory, thirty-four years later_, arXiv:1908.00488 [math.NT] (2019)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {ι : Type u_1} [Infinite ι], ∀ r > 0, Erdos26.IsThick fun x => r

references: [erdosproblems.com/26](https://www.erdosproblems.com/26)
[Te19](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1908.00488) G. Tenenbaum, _Some of Erdős' unconventional problems in number theory, thirty-four years later_, arXiv:1908.00488 [math.NT] (2019)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {ι : Type u_1} (A : ι → ℕ) {ε : ℝ}, 1 ≤ ε → Erdos26.IsWeaklyBehrend A ε

references: [erdosproblems.com/26](https://www.erdosproblems.com/26)
[Te19](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1908.00488) G. Tenenbaum, _Some of Erdős' unconventional problems in number theory, thirty-four years later_, arXiv:1908.00488 [math.NT] (2019)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {ι : Type u_1} (A : ι → ℕ), 1 ∈ Set.range A → Erdos26.MultiplesOf A = Set.univ

references: [erdosproblems.com/26](https://www.erdosproblems.com/26)
[Te19](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1908.00488) G. Tenenbaum, _Some of Erdős' unconventional problems in number theory, thirty-four years later_, arXiv:1908.00488 [math.NT] (2019)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {ι : Type u_1} [Finite ι] (A : ι → ℕ), ¬Erdos26.IsThick A

references: [erdosproblems.com/26](https://www.erdosproblems.com/26)
[Te19](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1908.00488) G. Tenenbaum, _Some of Erdős' unconventional problems in number theory, thirty-four years later_, arXiv:1908.00488 [math.NT] (2019)
[erdosproblems.com/26](https://www.erdosproblems.com/26)
[Te19](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1908.00488) G. Tenenbaum, _Some of Erdős' unconventional problems in number theory, thirty-four years later_, arXiv:1908.00488 [math.NT] (2019)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {ι : Type u_1} (A : ι → ℕ) {ε : ℝ}, ε < 0 → ¬Erdos26.IsWeaklyBehrend A ε

declarations.docstring:
Let $a_1 < a_2 < \cdots$ be an increasing sequence such that $\frac{a_n}{n} \to \infty$.
Is the sum $\sum_{n}^{\infty} \frac{a_n}{2^{a_n}}$ irrational?
references: [erdosproblems.com/260](https://www.erdosproblems.com/260)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (a : ℕ → ℤ) (s : ℝ),
    StrictMono a →
      Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(a n) / ↑n) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop →
        HasSum (fun n => ↑(a n) / 2 ^ a n) s → Irrational s

declarations.docstring: Is $a_n = 2^{2^n}$ an irrationality sequence in the above sense?
references: [erdosproblems.com/263](https://www.erdosproblems.com/263)

declarations.docstring:
Must every irrationality sequence $a_n$ in the above sense
satisfy $a_n^{1/n} \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$?

Note: this was answered **false** for the *pre-correction* statement, which did not
require monotonicity — the counterexample sequence is not increasing. The problem
was corrected on erdosproblems.com on 2026-04-02 to require increasing sequences;
for the corrected statement this question is **open**. The earlier formal proof
(for the pre-correction definition) is preserved at
https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/c8cf651906abe91051cf835d4232ad5648412113/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/263.lean#L298
references: [erdosproblems.com/263](https://www.erdosproblems.com/263)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ),
    Erdos263.IsIrrationalitySequence a → Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(a n) ^ (1 / ↑n)) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop

declarations.docstring:
Koizumi [Ko25] showed that $a_n = \lfloor \alpha^{2^n} \rfloor$ is an irrationality sequence
for all but countably many $\alpha > 1$.

[Ko25] Koizumi, J., Irrationality of the reciprocal sum of doubly exponential sequences,
       arXiv:2504.05933 (2025).
references: [erdosproblems.com/263](https://www.erdosproblems.com/263)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ᶠ (α : ℝ) in Filter.cocountable, α > 1 → Erdos263.IsIrrationalitySequence fun n => ⌊α ^ 2 ^ n⌋₊

declarations.docstring:
A folklore result states that any $a_n$ satisfying $\lim_{n \to \infty} a_n^{\frac{1}{2^n}} = \infty$
has $\sum \frac{1}{a_n}$ converging to an irrational number.
references: [erdosproblems.com/263](https://www.erdosproblems.com/263)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ),
  Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(a n) ^ (1 / 2 ^ n)) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop → Irrational (∑' (n : ℕ), 1 / ↑(a n))

declarations.docstring:
Kovač and Tao [KoTa24] proved that any strictly increasing sequence $a_n$ such that
$\sum \frac{1}{a_n}$ converges and $\lim \frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n^2} = 0$ is not
an irrationality sequence in the above sense.

[KoTa24] Kovač, V. and Tao T., On several irrationality problems for Ahmes series.
         arXiv:2406.17593 (2024).
references: [erdosproblems.com/263](https://www.erdosproblems.com/263)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ),
  StrictMono a →
    (Summable fun n => 1 / ↑(a n)) →
      Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(a (n + 1)) / ↑(a n) ^ 2) Filter.atTop (nhds 0) → ¬Erdos263.IsIrrationalitySequence a

declarations.docstring:
On the other hand, if there exists some $\varepsilon > 0$ such that $a_n$ satisfies
$\liminf \frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n^{2+\varepsilon}} > 0$, then $a_n$ is an irrationality sequence
by the above folklore result `erdos_263.variants.folklore`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/263](https://www.erdosproblems.com/263)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ),
  (∀ (n : ℕ), a n > 0) →
    StrictMono a →
      (∃ ε > 0, Filter.liminf (fun n => ↑(a (n + 1)) / ↑(a n) ^ (2 + ε)) Filter.atTop > 0) →
        Erdos263.IsIrrationalitySequence a

declarations.docstring:
Is $2^n$ an example of an irrationality sequence? Kovač and Tao proved that it is not [KoTa24]

[KoTa24] Kovač, V. and Tao T., On several irrationality problems for Ahmes series. arXiv:2406.17593 (2024).
references: [erdosproblems.com/264](https://www.erdosproblems.com/264)

declarations.docstring: Is $n!$ an example of an irrationality sequence?
references: [erdosproblems.com/264](https://www.erdosproblems.com/264)

declarations.docstring: One example is $2^{2^n}$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/264](https://www.erdosproblems.com/264)

declarations.docstring:
Kovač and Tao [KoTa24] generally proved that any strictly increasing sequence of positive integers
$a_n$ such that $\sum \frac{1}{a_n}$ converges and
$$
  \liminf_{n \to \infty} (a_n^2 \sum_{k > n} \frac{1}{a_k^2}) > 0
$$
is not an irrationality sequence.

[KoTa24] Kovač, V. and Tao T., On several irrationality problems for Ahmes series. arXiv:2406.17593 (2024).
references: [erdosproblems.com/264](https://www.erdosproblems.com/264)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {a : ℕ → ℕ},
  StrictMono a →
    0 ∉ Set.range a →
      (Summable fun x => 1 / ↑(a x)) →
        0 < Filter.liminf (fun n => ↑(a n) ^ 2 * ∑' (k : ↑(Set.Ioi n)), 1 / ↑(a ↑k) ^ 2) Filter.atTop →
          ¬Erdos264.IsIrrationalitySequence a

declarations.docstring:
On the other hand, Kovač and Tao [KoTa24] do prove that for any function $F$ with
$\lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{F(n + 1)}{F(n)} = \infty$ there exists such an irrationality sequence with $a_n \sim F(n)$.

[KoTa24] Kovač, V. and Tao T., On several irrationality problems for Ahmes series. arXiv:2406.17593 (2024).
references: [erdosproblems.com/264](https://www.erdosproblems.com/264)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {F : ℕ → ℕ},
  Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(F (n + 1)) / ↑(F n)) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop →
    ∃ a, Erdos264.IsIrrationalitySequence a ∧ Asymptotics.IsEquivalent Filter.atTop (fun n => ↑(a n)) fun n => ↑(F n)

declarations.docstring:
Let $a_n$ be an infinite sequence of positive integers such that $\sum \frac{1}{a_n}$ converges.
There exists some integer $t \ge 1$ such that $\sum \frac{1}{a_n + t}$ is irrational.

This was disproven by Kovač and Tao in [KoTa24].

[KoTa24] Kovač, V. and Tao T., On several irrationality problems for Ahmes series.
         [arXiv:2406.17593](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.17593) (2024).
references: [erdosproblems.com/266](https://www.erdosproblems.com/266)
declarations.type_pretty:
¬∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ),
    ((∀ (n : ℕ), a n ≥ 1) ∧ Summable fun x => 1 / ↑(a x)) → ∃ t ≥ 1, Irrational (∑' (n : ℕ), 1 / (↑(a n) + ↑t))

declarations.docstring:
In fact, Kovač and Tao proved in [KoTa24] that there exists a strictly increasing
sequence $a_n$ of positive integers such that $\sum \frac{1}{a_n + t}$ converges to a rational
number for all $t \in \mathbb{Q}$ such that $t \ne -a_n$ for any $n$.

[KoTa24] Kovač, V. and Tao T., On several irrationality problems for Ahmes series.
         [arXiv:2406.17593](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.17593) (2024).
references: [erdosproblems.com/266](https://www.erdosproblems.com/266)
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ a, StrictMono a ∧ a 0 ≥ 1 ∧ ∀ (t : ℚ), (¬∃ n, t = -↑(a n)) → ∃ q, HasSum (fun n => 1 / (↑(a n) + ↑t)) ↑q

declarations.docstring:
Let $F_1=F_2=1$ and $F_{n+1} = F_n + F_{n-1}$ be the Fibonacci sequence.
Let $n_1 < n_2 < \dots$ be an infinite sequence with $\frac{n_{k+1}}{n_k} \ge c > 1$. Must
$\sum_k \frac 1 {F_{n_k}}$ be irrational?
references: [erdosproblems.com/267](https://www.erdosproblems.com/267)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (n : ℕ → ℕ),
    ∀ c > 1, StrictMono n → (∀ (k : ℕ), c ≤ ↑(n (k + 1)) / ↑(n k)) → Irrational (∑' (k : ℕ), 1 / ↑(Nat.fib (n k)))

declarations.docstring:
The sum $\sum_n \frac 1 {F_{n}}$ itself was proved to be irrational by André-Jeannin.

Ref: André-Jeannin, Richard, _Irrationalité de la somme des inverses de certaines suites récurrentes_.
references: [erdosproblems.com/267](https://www.erdosproblems.com/267)

declarations.docstring:
Let $F_1=F_2=1$ and $F_{n+1} = F_n + F_{n-1}$ be the Fibonacci sequence.
Let $n_1 < n_2 < \dots$ be an infinite sequence with $\frac {n_k}{k} \to \infty$. Must
$\sum_k \frac 1 {F_{n_k}}$ be irrational?
references: [erdosproblems.com/267](https://www.erdosproblems.com/267)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (n : ℕ → ℕ),
    StrictMono n →
      Filter.Tendsto (fun k => ↑(n (k + 1)) / ↑k.succ) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop →
        Irrational (∑' (k : ℕ), 1 / ↑(Nat.fib (n k)))

declarations.docstring:
Good [Go74] and Bicknell and Hoggatt [BiHo76] have shown that $\sum_n \frac 1 {F_{2^n}}$ is irrational.


Formal proof provided by AlphaProof
Ref:
* [Go74] Good, I. J., _A reciprocal series of Fibonacci numbers_
* [BiHo76] Hoggatt, Jr., V. E. and Bicknell, Marjorie, _A reciprocal series of Fibonacci numbers with subscripts $2\sp{n}k$_
references: [erdosproblems.com/267](https://www.erdosproblems.com/267)

declarations.docstring:
Let `X` be the set of points in `Fin d → ℝ` of the shape
`fun i : Fin d => ∑' n : A, (1 : ℝ) / (n + i)` for some infinite subset `A ⊆ ℕ` such that
`1 / n` is summable over `A`. `X` has nonempty interior. This is proved in [KoTa24].
-
references: [erdosproblems.com/268](https://www.erdosproblems.com/268)
[KoTa24] Kova\vC, V. and Tao T., On several irrationality problems for Ahmes series.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (d : ℕ),
  (interior {x | ∃ A, A.Infinite ∧ (Summable fun n => 1 / ↑↑n) ∧ x = fun i => ∑' (n : ↑A), 1 / (↑↑n + ↑↑i)}).Nonempty

declarations.docstring:
This theorem addresses the case where the set of primes $P$ is infinite. In this case the sum is
irrational.
references: [erdosproblems.com/269](https://www.erdosproblems.com/269)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (P : Set ℕ), (∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p) → P.Infinite → Irrational (Erdos269.series P)

declarations.docstring:
Let $P$ be a finite set of primes with $|P| \ge 2$ and let
$\{a_1 < a_2 < \dots\}$ be the set of positive integers whose prime factors
are all in $P$. Is the sum
$$ \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{[a_1,\ldots,a_n]} $$
irrational?
references: [erdosproblems.com/269](https://www.erdosproblems.com/269)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ (P : Finset ℕ), (∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p) → P.card ≥ 2 → Irrational (Erdos269.series ↑P)

declarations.docstring:
Let $P$ be a finite set of primes with $|P| \ge 2$ and let
$\{a_1 < a_2 < \dots\}$ be the set of positive integers whose prime factors
are all in $P$. Is the sum
$$ \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{[a_1,\ldots,a_n]} $$
rational?
references: [erdosproblems.com/269](https://www.erdosproblems.com/269)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ (P : Finset ℕ), (∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p) → P.card ≥ 2 → ∃ q, ↑q = Erdos269.series ↑P

declarations.docstring:
Let $N\geq 1$. What is the largest $t$ such that there are
$A_1,\ldots,A_t\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ with $A_i\cap A_j$ a non-empty
arithmetic progression for all $i\neq j$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/272](https://www.erdosproblems.com/272)

declarations.docstring: Simonovits and Sós have shown that $t\ll N^2$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/272](https://www.erdosproblems.com/272)

declarations.docstring:
Szabo showed that the maximal $t$ is equal to
$$
  \frac{N^2}{2} + O(N^{5/3}\log^3N).
$$
references: [erdosproblems.com/272](https://www.erdosproblems.com/272)

declarations.docstring:
Szabo asks whether the maximal $t$ is given by
$$
  \frac{N^2}{2} + O(N)
$$
references: [erdosproblems.com/272](https://www.erdosproblems.com/272)

declarations.docstring: Is there a covering system all of whose moduli are of the form $p-1$ for some primes $p \geq 5$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/273](https://www.erdosproblems.com/273)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∃ c, ∀ (i : c.ι), ∃ p, Nat.Prime p ∧ 5 ≤ p ∧ c.moduli i = Ideal.span {↑(p - 1)}

declarations.docstring: Is there a covering system all of whose moduli are of the form $p-1$ for some primes $p \geq 3$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/273](https://www.erdosproblems.com/273)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∃ c, ∀ (i : c.ι), ∃ p, Nat.Prime p ∧ 3 ≤ p ∧ c.moduli i = Ideal.span {p - 1}

declarations.docstring:
If $G$ is a group, can there exist an exact covering of $G$ by more than one coset
of different sizes? (i.e. each element is contained in exactly one of the cosets.)

The conjectured answer is no: in every such exact covering, two of the subgroups have
the same cardinality.
references: [erdosproblems.com/274](https://www.erdosproblems.com/274)
[Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herzog%E2%80%93Sch%C3%B6nheim_conjecture)
[arXiv:1803.08301](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.08301)
[arXiv:1803.03569](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.03569)
[PMC7247885](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7247885/)
[arXiv:1804.11103](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.11103)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (G : Type u_1) [inst : Group G],
    1 < ENat.card G →
      ∀ (ι : Type u_2) [inst_1 : Fintype ι] (P : Erdos274.Group.ExactCovering G ι),
        1 < Fintype.card ι → ∃ i j, i ≠ j ∧ Cardinal.mk ↥(P.parts i) = Cardinal.mk ↥(P.parts j)

declarations.docstring:
If `G` is a finite abelian group then there cannot exist an exact covering of `G` by more
than one cosets of different sizes? (i.e. each element is contained in exactly one
of the cosets.)
references: [erdosproblems.com/274](https://www.erdosproblems.com/274)
[Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herzog%E2%80%93Sch%C3%B6nheim_conjecture)
[arXiv:1803.08301](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.08301)
[arXiv:1803.03569](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.03569)
[PMC7247885](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7247885/)
[arXiv:1804.11103](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.11103)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {G : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype G] [inst_1 : CommGroup G],
  1 < Fintype.card G →
    ∀ {ι : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype ι] (P : Erdos274.Group.ExactCovering G ι),
      1 < Fintype.card ι → ∃ i j, i ≠ j ∧ Cardinal.mk ↥(P.parts i) = Cardinal.mk ↥(P.parts j)

declarations.docstring:
Let $G$ be a group, and let $A = \{a_1G_1, \dots, a_kG_k\}$ be a finite system of left cosets of
subgroups $G_1, \dots, G_k$ of $G$.

Herzog and Schönheim conjectured that if $A$ forms a partition of $G$ with $k > 1$, then the
indices $[G:G_1], \dots, [G:G_k]$ cannot be distinct.
references: [erdosproblems.com/274](https://www.erdosproblems.com/274)
[Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herzog%E2%80%93Sch%C3%B6nheim_conjecture)
[arXiv:1803.08301](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.08301)
[arXiv:1803.03569](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.03569)
[PMC7247885](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7247885/)
[arXiv:1804.11103](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.11103)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {G : Type u_1} [inst : Group G],
  1 < ENat.card G →
    ∀ {ι : Type u_2} [inst_1 : Fintype ι],
      1 < Fintype.card ι →
        ∀ (P : Erdos274.Group.ExactCovering G ι), ∃ i j, i ≠ j ∧ (P.parts i).index = (P.parts j).index

declarations.docstring:
If a finite system of $r$ congruences $\{ a_i\pmod{n_i} : 1\leq i\leq r\}$ (the $n_i$ are not
necessarily distinct) covers $2^r$ consecutive integers then it covers all integers.

This is best possible as the system $2^{i-1}\pmod{2^i}$ shows. This was proved independently by
Selfridge and Crittenden and Vanden Eynden [CrVE70].

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev using Aristotle.
references: [erdosproblems.com/275](https://www.erdosproblems.com/275)
[CrVE70] R.B. Crittenden and C.L. Vanden Eynden, *Any n arithmetic progressions covering the first 2^n integers cover all integers*, Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 24 (1970), 475-481.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (r : ℕ) (a : Fin r → ℤ) (n : Fin r → ℕ),
  (∃ k, ∀ x ∈ Set.Ico k (k + 2 ^ r), ∃ i, x ≡ a i [ZMOD ↑(n i)]) → ∀ (x : ℤ), ∃ i, x ≡ a i [ZMOD ↑(n i)]

declarations.docstring:
Is there an infinite Lucas sequence $a_0, a_1, \ldots$ where $a_{n+2} = a_{n+1} + a_n$ for
$n \ge 0$ such that all $a_k$ are composite, and yet no integer has a common factor with every
term of the sequence?
references: [erdosproblems.com/276](https://www.erdosproblems.com/276)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∃ a, Erdos276.IsLucasSequence a ∧ (∀ (k : ℕ), (a k).Composite) ∧ ∀ n > 1, ∃ k, n.gcd (a k) = 1

declarations.docstring:
Is it true that, for every $c$, there exists an $n$ such that $\sigma(n)>cn$ but there is no
covering system whose moduli all divide $n$?

This was answered affirmatively by Haight [Ha79].
references: [erdosproblems.com/277](https://www.erdosproblems.com/277)
[Ha79] Haight, J. A., Covering systems of congruences, a negative result. Mathematika (1979), 53--61.
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ (c : ℝ), ∃ n, ↑((ArithmeticFunction.sigma 1) n) > c * ↑n ∧ ∀ (m : StrictCoveringSystem ℤ), ∃ i, ↑n ∉ m.moduli i

declarations.docstring:
Let $k\geq 3$. Is there a choice of congruence classes $a_p\pmod{p}$ for every prime $p$
such that all sufficiently large integers can be written as $a_p+tp$ for some prime $p$
and integer $t\geq k$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/279](https://www.erdosproblems.com/279)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ k ≥ 3, ∃ a N, (∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → a p < p) ∧ ∀ n ≥ N, ∃ p, ∃ t ≥ k, Nat.Prime p ∧ n = a p + t * p

declarations.docstring:
If $A ⊆ \mathbb{N}$ is such that $A + A$ contains all but finitely many integers then
$\limsup 1_A ∗ 1_A(n) = \infty$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/28](https://www.erdosproblems.com/28)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (A : Set ℕ), (A + A)ᶜ.Finite → Filter.limsup (fun n => ↑(AdditiveCombinatorics.sumRep A n)) Filter.atTop = ⊤

declarations.docstring:
Let $n_1<n_2<\cdots $ be an infinite sequence of integers with associated $a_k\pmod{n_k}$, such that for some $\epsilon>0$ we have $n_k>(1+\epsilon)k\log k$ for all $k$. Then
$$
\#\{ m<n_k : m\not\equiv a_i\pmod{n_i} \textrm{ for }1\leq i\leq k\}\neq o(k).
$$

Cambie observed that this is false.
references: [erdosproblems.com/280](https://www.erdosproblems.com/280)
[ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
declarations.type_pretty:
False ↔
  ∀ (n a : ℕ → ℕ),
    StrictMono n →
      (∀ (i : ℕ), 1 ≤ i → a i < n i) →
        (∃ ε, 0 < ε ∧ ∀ (k : ℕ), 1 ≤ k → ↑(n k) > (1 + ε) * ↑k * Real.log ↑k) →
          ¬Filter.Tendsto (fun k => ↑(Erdos280.uncoveredCount n a k) / ↑k) Filter.atTop (nhds 0)

declarations.docstring:
Let $n_1<n_2<\cdots$ be an infinite sequence such that, for any choice of congruence classes
$a_i\pmod{n_i}$, the set of integers not satisfying any of the congruences $a_i\pmod{n_i}$ has
density $0$. Is it true that for every $\epsilon>0$ there exists some $k$ such that, for every
choice of congruence classes $a_i$, the density of integers not satisfying any of the congruences
$a_i\pmod{n_i}$ for $1\leq i\leq k$ is less than $\epsilon$?

The answer is yes; the linked Lean proof formalizes Somani's argument.
references: [erdosproblems.com/281](https://www.erdosproblems.com/281)
[ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
[DaEr36] Davenport, H. and Erdős, P., *On sequences of positive integers*. Acta Arithmetica (1936), 147-151.
[HaRo66] Halberstam, H. and Roth, K. F., *Sequences. Vol. I*. (1966), xx+291.
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (n : ℕ → ℕ),
    StrictMono n →
      (∀ (i : ℕ), 0 < n i) →
        (∀ (a : Erdos281.ResidueChoice n), (Erdos281.avoidAll n a).HasIntDensity 0) →
          ∀ (ε : ℝ),
            0 < ε → ∃ k, ∀ (a : Erdos281.ResidueChoice n), ∃ d, (Erdos281.avoidPrefix n a k).HasIntDensity d ∧ d < ε

declarations.docstring:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set and consider the following
greedy algorithm for a rational $x\in (0,1)$: choose the minimal $n\in A$ such
that $n\geq 1/x$ and repeat with $x$ replaced by $x-\frac{1}{n}$. If this
terminates after finitely many steps then this produces a representation of
$x$ as the sum of distinct unit fractions with denominators from $A$.

Does this process always terminate if $x$ has odd denominator and $A$ is the
set of odd numbers?
references: [erdosproblems.com/282](https://www.erdosproblems.com/282)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {x : ℚ}, x ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1 → Odd x.den → Erdos282.greedyUnitFractionRem {n | Odd n} x =ᶠ[Filter.atTop] 0

declarations.docstring: In 1202 Fibonacci observed that this process terminates for any $x$ when $A=\mathbb{N}$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/282](https://www.erdosproblems.com/282)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {x : ℚ}, x ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1 → Erdos282.greedyUnitFractionRem Set.univ x =ᶠ[Filter.atTop] 0

declarations.docstring: More generally, for which pairs $x$ and $A$ does this process terminate?
references: [erdosproblems.com/282](https://www.erdosproblems.com/282)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (x : ℚ) (A : Set ℕ), Erdos282.greedyUnitFractionRem A x =ᶠ[Filter.atTop] 0 ↔ (x, A) ∈ sorry

declarations.docstring:
Graham has shown that $\frac{m}{n}$ is the sum of distinct unit fractions
with denominators $\equiv a\pmod{d}$ if and only if
$$\left(\frac{n}{(n,a,d)},\frac{d}{(a,d)}\right)=1.$$
Does the greedy algorithm always
terminate in such cases?
references: [erdosproblems.com/282](https://www.erdosproblems.com/282)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {x : ℚ},
  x ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1 →
    ∀ {a d : ℕ},
      1 < d →
        (x.den / x.den.gcd (a.gcd d)).gcd (d / a.gcd d) = 1 →
          (Erdos282.greedyUnitFractionRem {n | n ≡ a [MOD d]} x =ᶠ[Filter.atTop] 0 ↔ True)

declarations.docstring:
Graham has also shown that $x$ is the sum of distinct unit fractions with
square denominators if and only if $x\in [0,\pi^2/6-1)\cup [1,\pi^2/6)$. Does the
greedy algorithm for this always terminate? Erdős and Graham believe not - indeed, perhaps it
fails to terminate almost always.
references: [erdosproblems.com/282](https://www.erdosproblems.com/282)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (x : ℚ),
    ↑x ∈ Set.Ico 0 (Real.pi ^ 2 / 6 - 1) ∪ Set.Ico 1 (Real.pi ^ 2 / 6) →
      Erdos282.greedyUnitFractionRem {n | IsSquare n} x =ᶠ[Filter.atTop] 0

references: [erdosproblems.com/282](https://www.erdosproblems.com/282)
[erdosproblems.com/282](https://www.erdosproblems.com/282)
[erdosproblems.com/282](https://www.erdosproblems.com/282)

declarations.docstring:
Let $p\colon \mathbb{Z} \rightarrow \mathbb{Z}$ be a polynomial whose leading coefficient is
positive and such that there exists no $d≥2$ with $d ∣ p(n)$ for all $n≥1$. Is it true that,
for all sufficiently large $m$, there exist integers $1≤n_1<\dots < n_k$ such that
$$1=\frac{1}{n_1}+\cdots+\frac{1}{n_k}$$
and
$$m=p(n_1)+\cdots+p(n_k)$$?

GPT 5.5 Pro (prompted by Price) has given a proof that the answer is yes, for the stronger version
with $1$ replaced by any rational $\alpha>0$.

This was formalized in Lean by Ammanamanchi using Opus 4.6 and GPT 5.5 Pro.
references: [erdosproblems.com/283](https://www.erdosproblems.com/283)
[Al19] Alekseyev, Max A., On partitions into squares of distinct integers whose

declarations.docstring: Alekseyev [Al19] has proved this when $p(x)=x^2$, for all $m>8542$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/283](https://www.erdosproblems.com/283)
[Al19] Alekseyev, Max A., On partitions into squares of distinct integers whose

declarations.docstring: Burr has proved this if $p(x)=x^k$ with $k\geq 1$ and if we allow $n_i=n_j$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/283](https://www.erdosproblems.com/283)
[Al19] Alekseyev, Max A., On partitions into squares of distinct integers whose
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ k ≥ 1,
  ∀ᶠ (m : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
    ∃ M,
      (∀ n ∈ M, 1 ≤ n) ∧
        (Multiset.map (fun n => 1 / n) do
                let a ← M
                pure ↑a).sum =
            1 ∧
          (Multiset.map (fun n => n ^ k) do
                let a ← M
                pure ↑a).sum =
            ↑m

Cassels [Ca60] has proved that these conditions on the polynomial imply every sufficiently large
integer is the sum of $p(n_i)$ with distinct $n_i$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/283](https://www.erdosproblems.com/283)
[Al19] Alekseyev, Max A., On partitions into squares of distinct integers whose
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (p : Polynomial ℤ),
  0 < p.leadingCoeff →
    (¬∃ d ≥ 2, ∀ n ≥ 1, d ∣ Polynomial.eval n p) →
      ∀ᶠ (m : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ S, (∀ n ∈ S, 1 ≤ n) ∧ ∑ n ∈ S, Polynomial.eval (↑n) p = ↑m

declarations.docstring: Graham [Gr63] has proved this when $p(x)=x$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/283](https://www.erdosproblems.com/283)
[Al19] Alekseyev, Max A., On partitions into squares of distinct integers whose

declarations.docstring:
Graham also conjectures that this remains true with $1$ replaced by an arbitrary rational $\alpha>0$
(provided $m$ is taken sufficiently large depending on $\alpha$).
references: [erdosproblems.com/283](https://www.erdosproblems.com/283)
[Al19] Alekseyev, Max A., On partitions into squares of distinct integers whose
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (p : Polynomial ℤ) (α : ℚ),
  0 < p.leadingCoeff →

      α > 0 →
        ∀ᶠ (m : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ S, (∀ n ∈ S, 1 ≤ n) ∧ ∑ n ∈ S, 1 / ↑n = α ∧ ∑ n ∈ S, Polynomial.eval (↑n) p = ↑m

declarations.docstring:
van Doorn [vD25] has investigated the question of what 'sufficiently large' means for $p(x)=x$.
van Doorn has also proved the original conjecture for many linear and quadratic polynomials.
For example, if $p(x) = x + b$ with $1 \leq b \leq 5000$, then the conjecture is true.
references: [erdosproblems.com/283](https://www.erdosproblems.com/283)
[Al19] Alekseyev, Max A., On partitions into squares of distinct integers whose
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (b : ℤ), 1 ≤ b → b ≤ 5000 → Erdos283.Condition (Polynomial.X + Polynomial.C b)

van Doorn [vD25] has proved the original conjecture for many linear and quadratic polynomials.
For example, if $p(x) = x^2 + b$ with $1 \leq b \leq 800$, then the conjecture is true.

[Al19] Alekseyev, Max A., On partitions into squares of distinct integers whose
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (b : ℤ), 1 ≤ b → b ≤ 800 → Erdos283.Condition (Polynomial.X ^ 2 + Polynomial.C b)

declarations.docstring:
Let $f(k)$ be the minimal value of $n_k$ such that there exist $n_1 < n_2 < \dots < n_k$ with
$$
  1 = \frac{1}{n_1} + \cdots + \frac{1}{n_k}.
$$
Is it true that
$$
  f(k) = (1 + o(1)) \frac{e}{e - 1} k ?
$$

Proved by Martin [Ma00].

[Ma00] Martin, Greg, _Denser Egyptian fractions_. Acta Arith. (2000), 231-260.
references: [erdosproblems.com/285](https://www.erdosproblems.com/285)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (f : ℕ → ℕ) (S : Set ℕ),
    S = {k | ∃ n, StrictMono n ∧ 0 ∉ Set.range n ∧ 1 = ∑ i, 1 / ↑(n i)} →
      (∀ k ∈ S,
          IsLeast {x | ∃ n, ∃ (_ : StrictMono n) (_ : 0 ∉ Set.range n) (_ : 1 = ∑ i, 1 / ↑(n i)), n (Fin.last k) = x}
            (f k)) →
        ∃ o, ∃ (_ : o =o[Filter.atTop] 1), ∀ k ∈ S, ↑(f k) = (1 + o k) * Real.exp 1 / (Real.exp 1 - 1) * (↑k + 1)

declarations.docstring: It is trivial that $f(k)\geq (1 + o(1)) \frac{e}{e - 1}k$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/285](https://www.erdosproblems.com/285)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (f : ℕ → ℕ) (S : Set ℕ),
  S = {k | ∃ n, StrictMono n ∧ 0 ∉ Set.range n ∧ 1 = ∑ i, 1 / ↑(n i)} →
    (∀ k ∈ S,
        IsLeast {x | ∃ n, ∃ (_ : StrictMono n) (_ : 0 ∉ Set.range n) (_ : 1 = ∑ i, 1 / ↑(n i)), n (Fin.last k) = x}
          (f k)) →
      ∃ o, ∃ (_ : o =o[Filter.atTop] 1), ∀ k ∈ S, (1 + o k) * Real.exp 1 / (Real.exp 1 - 1) * (↑k + 1) ≤ ↑(f k)

declarations.docstring:
Let $k\geq2$. Is it true that, for any distinct integers
$1 < n_1 < \cdots < n_k$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^k \frac{1}{n_i} = 1$,
we must have $\max(n_{i+1} - n_i) \geq 3$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/287](https://www.erdosproblems.com/287)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (s : Fin k → ℕ), StrictMono s → 1 < s ⟨0, ⋯⟩ → ∑ i, 1 / ↑(s i) = 1 → 3 ≤ Erdos287.max_gap k s

declarations.docstring:
The example $1 = \frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{6}$ shows that $3$ would be best possible here:
the sequence $(2, 3, 6)$ is a valid Egyptian fraction representation of $1$ with
`max_gap = 3`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/287](https://www.erdosproblems.com/287)
declarations.type_pretty:
have s := ![2, 3, 6];
StrictMono s ∧ 1 < s 0 ∧ ∑ i, 1 / ↑(s i) = 1 ∧ Erdos287.max_gap 3 s = 3

declarations.docstring:
The lower bound of $\geq 2$ is equivalent to saying that $1$ is not the sum of reciprocals of
consecutive integers, proved by Erdős [Er32].
references: [erdosproblems.com/287](https://www.erdosproblems.com/287)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (k : ℕ) (x : 2 ≤ k) (s : Fin k → ℕ), StrictMono s → 1 < s ⟨0, ⋯⟩ → ∑ i, 1 / ↑(s i) = 1 → 2 ≤ Erdos287.max_gap k s

declarations.docstring:
For all large $N$, there exists a prime $p \in [N, 2N]$ such that $\frac{p+1}{2}$ is also prime.

This is an open conjecture. If true, it would imply `erdos_287` for all but at most finitely
many exceptions (see `erdos_287.variants.prime_conjecture_implies`).
references: [erdosproblems.com/287](https://www.erdosproblems.com/287)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∃ N₀, ∀ (N : ℕ), N₀ ≤ N → ∃ p, Nat.Prime p ∧ N ≤ p ∧ p ≤ 2 * N ∧ Nat.Prime ((p + 1) / 2)

declarations.docstring:
The conjecture `erdos_287` would follow for all but at most finitely many exceptions if it were
known that, for all large $N$, there exists a prime $p \in [N, 2N]$ such that $\frac{p+1}{2}$
is also prime.

More precisely: if the prime conjecture holds, then there exists $k_0$ such that for all
$k \geq k_0$, any Egyptian fraction representation of $1$ with $k$ terms and all terms $> 1$
must have $\max(n_{i+1} - n_i) \geq 3$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/287](https://www.erdosproblems.com/287)
declarations.type_pretty:
(True ↔ ∃ N₀, ∀ (N : ℕ), N₀ ≤ N → ∃ p, Nat.Prime p ∧ N ≤ p ∧ p ≤ 2 * N ∧ Nat.Prime ((p + 1) / 2)) →
  ∃ k₀,
    ∀ (k : ℕ),
      k₀ ≤ k →
        ∀ (hk : 2 ≤ k) (s : Fin k → ℕ), StrictMono s → 1 < s ⟨0, ⋯⟩ → ∑ i, 1 / ↑(s i) = 1 → 3 ≤ Erdos287.max_gap k s

declarations.docstring:
Is it true that there are only finitely many pairs of intervals $I_1$, $I_2$ such that
$$
\sum_{n_1 \in I_1} \frac{1}{n_1} + \sum_{n_2 \in I_2} \frac{1}{n_2} \in \mathbb{N}?
$$
references: [erdosproblems.com/288](https://www.erdosproblems.com/288)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  {I | ∀ (j : Fin 2), (I j).1 ≤ (I j).2 ∧ ∃ n, ∑ j, ∑ nⱼ ∈ (Set.Icc (I j).1 (I j).2).toFinset, (↑↑nⱼ)⁻¹ = ↑↑n}.Finite

declarations.docstring: Is it true for any $k > 2$ that only finitely many $k$ intervals satisfy this condition?
references: [erdosproblems.com/288](https://www.erdosproblems.com/288)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∃ k > 2,
    {I | ∀ (j : Fin k), (I j).1 ≤ (I j).2 ∧ ∃ n, ∑ j, ∑ nⱼ ∈ (Set.Icc (I j).1 (I j).2).toFinset, (↑↑nⱼ)⁻¹ = ↑↑n}.Finite

declarations.docstring: This is still open even if $|I_2| = 1$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/288](https://www.erdosproblems.com/288)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ {(I, n₂) | I.1 ≤ I.2 ∧ ∃ n, ∑ n₁ ∈ (Set.Icc I.1 I.2).toFinset, (↑↑n₁)⁻¹ + (↑↑n₂)⁻¹ = ↑↑n}.Finite

declarations.docstring: It is perhaps true with two intervals replaced by any $k$ intervals.
references: [erdosproblems.com/288](https://www.erdosproblems.com/288)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (k : ℕ),
    {I | ∀ (j : Fin k), (I j).1 ≤ (I j).2 ∧ ∃ n, ∑ j, ∑ nⱼ ∈ (Set.Icc (I j).1 (I j).2).toFinset, (↑↑nⱼ)⁻¹ = ↑↑n}.Finite

declarations.docstring:
Is it true that, for all sufficiently large $k$, there exists finite intervals
$I_1, \dotsc, I_k \subset \mathbb{N}$ with $|I_i| \geq 2$ for $1 \leq i \leq k$ such that
$$
1 = \sum_{i=1}^k \sum_{n \in I_i} \frac{1}{n}.
$$
references: [erdosproblems.com/289](https://www.erdosproblems.com/289)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ᶠ (k : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
    ∃ I,
      (∀ (i : Fin k), (I i).1 < (I i).2) ∧
        (∀ (i j : Fin k), i ≠ j → (I i).2 < (I j).1 ∨ (I j).2 < (I i).1) ∧
          ∑ i, ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc (I i).1 (I i).2, (↑n)⁻¹ = 1

declarations.docstring:
Let $a\geq 1$. Must there exist some $b>a$ such that
$$\sum_{a\leq n\leq b}\frac{1}{n}=\frac{r_1}{s_1}\textrm{ and }
\sum_{a\leq n\leq b+1}\frac{1}{n}=\frac{r_2}{s_2},$$
with $(r_i,s_i)=1$ and $s_2<s_1$? If so, how does this $b(a)$ grow with $a$?

This was resolved in the affirmative by van Doorn [vD24], who proved $b=b(a)$ always exists, and in
fact $b(a) \ll a$. Indeed, if $a\in (3^k,3^{k+1}]$ then one can take $b=2\cdot 3^{k+1}-1$. van Doorn
also proves that $b(a)>a+(1/2-o(1))\log a$, and considers various generalisations of the original
problem.
references: [erdosproblems.com/290](https://www.erdosproblems.com/290)
[ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathématique (1980), p.34.
[vD24] van Doorn, W., *On the non-monotonicity of the denominator of generalized harmonic sums*. arXiv:2411.03073 (2024).
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ (a : ℕ), 1 ≤ a → ∃ b, a < b ∧ Erdos290.harmonicDen a (b + 1) < Erdos290.harmonicDen a b

references: [erdosproblems.com/291](https://www.erdosproblems.com/291)
[ErGr80, p.34] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
[Sh16] P. Shiu, The denominators of harmonic numbers. arXiv:1607.02863 (2016).
[WuYa22] Wu, Bing-Ling and Yan, Xiao-Hui, On the denominators of harmonic numbers. {IV}. C. R. Math. Acad. Sci. Paris (2022), 53--57.
[erdosproblems.com/291](https://www.erdosproblems.com/291)
[ErGr80, p.34] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
[Sh16] P. Shiu, The denominators of harmonic numbers. arXiv:1607.02863 (2016).
[WuYa22] Wu, Bing-Ling and Yan, Xiao-Hui, On the denominators of harmonic numbers. {IV}. C. R. Math. Acad. Sci. Paris (2022), 53--57.

declarations.docstring:
Let $n\geq 1$ and define $L_n$ to be the least common multiple of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and $a_n$ by
$\sum_{1\leq k\leq n}\frac{1}{k}=\frac{a_n}{L_n}$.

Is it true that $(a_n,L_n)=1$ occurs for infinitely many $n$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/291](https://www.erdosproblems.com/291)
[ErGr80, p.34] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
[Sh16] P. Shiu, The denominators of harmonic numbers. arXiv:1607.02863 (2016).
[WuYa22] Wu, Bing-Ling and Yan, Xiao-Hui, On the denominators of harmonic numbers. {IV}. C. R. Math. Acad. Sci. Paris (2022), 53--57.

declarations.docstring:
Is it true that $(a_n,L_n)>1$ occurs for infinitely many $n$?

Steinerberger has observed that the answer to the second question is trivially yes: for example, any
$n$ which begins with a $2$ in base $3$ has $3\mid (a_n,L_n)$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/291](https://www.erdosproblems.com/291)
[ErGr80, p.34] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
[Sh16] P. Shiu, The denominators of harmonic numbers. arXiv:1607.02863 (2016).
[WuYa22] Wu, Bing-Ling and Yan, Xiao-Hui, On the denominators of harmonic numbers. {IV}. C. R. Math. Acad. Sci. Paris (2022), 53--57.

declarations.docstring:
This leads to a heuristic prediction (see for example a preprint of Shiu [Sh16]) of
$\asymp\frac{x}{\log x}$ for the number of $n\in [1,x]$ such that $(a_n,L_n)=1$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/291](https://www.erdosproblems.com/291)
[ErGr80, p.34] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
[Sh16] P. Shiu, The denominators of harmonic numbers. arXiv:1607.02863 (2016).
[WuYa22] Wu, Bing-Ling and Yan, Xiao-Hui, On the denominators of harmonic numbers. {IV}. C. R. Math. Acad. Sci. Paris (2022), 53--57.
declarations.type_pretty: (fun x => ↑{n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 x | (Erdos291.a n).gcd (Erdos291.L n) = 1}.card) =Θ[Filter.atTop] fun x => ↑x / Real.log ↑x

declarations.docstring:
In particular, there should be infinitely many $n$, but the set of such $n$ should have
density zero. Unfortunately this heuristic is difficult to turn into a proof.
references: [erdosproblems.com/291](https://www.erdosproblems.com/291)
[ErGr80, p.34] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
[Sh16] P. Shiu, The denominators of harmonic numbers. arXiv:1607.02863 (2016).
[WuYa22] Wu, Bing-Ling and Yan, Xiao-Hui, On the denominators of harmonic numbers. {IV}. C. R. Math. Acad. Sci. Paris (2022), 53--57.
declarations.type_pretty: Filter.Tendsto (fun N => ↑{n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N | (Erdos291.a n).gcd (Erdos291.L n) = 1}.card / ↑N) Filter.atTop (nhds 0)

declarations.docstring:
More generally, if the leading digit of $n$ in base $p$ is $p-1$ then $p\mid (a_n,L_n)$. There is
in fact a necessary and sufficient condition: a prime $p\leq n$ divides $(a_n,L_n)$ if and only if
$p$ divides the numerator of $1+\cdots+\frac{1}{k}$, where $k$ is the leading digit of $n$ in base
$p$. This can be seen by writing $a_n = \frac{L_n}{1}+\cdots+\frac{L_n}{n}$ and observing that the
right-hand side is congruent to $1+\cdots+1/k$ modulo $p$. (The previous claim about $p-1$ follows
immediately from Wolstenholme's theorem.)
references: [erdosproblems.com/291](https://www.erdosproblems.com/291)
[ErGr80, p.34] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
[Sh16] P. Shiu, The denominators of harmonic numbers. arXiv:1607.02863 (2016).
[WuYa22] Wu, Bing-Ling and Yan, Xiao-Hui, On the denominators of harmonic numbers. {IV}. C. R. Math. Acad. Sci. Paris (2022), 53--57.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (n p : ℕ),
  Nat.Prime p →
    p ≤ n →
      have k := n / p ^ Nat.log p n;
      p ∣ (Erdos291.a n).gcd (Erdos291.L n) ↔ ↑p ∣ (∑ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, 1 / ↑i).num

declarations.docstring:
Wu and Yan [WuYa22] have proved, conditional on $\frac{1}{\log p}$ being linearly independent
over $\mathbb{Q}$ for any finite collection of primes $p$ (itself a consequence of Schanuel's
conjecture), that the set of $n$ for which $(a_n,L_n)>1$ has upper density $1$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/291](https://www.erdosproblems.com/291)
[ErGr80, p.34] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
[Sh16] P. Shiu, The denominators of harmonic numbers. arXiv:1607.02863 (2016).
[WuYa22] Wu, Bing-Ling and Yan, Xiao-Hui, On the denominators of harmonic numbers. {IV}. C. R. Math. Acad. Sci. Paris (2022), 53--57.
declarations.type_pretty:
(LinearIndependent ℚ fun p => 1 / Real.log ↑↑p) →
  Filter.limsup (fun N => ↑↑{n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N | (Erdos291.a n).gcd (Erdos291.L n) > 1}.card / ↑↑N) Filter.atTop = 1

declarations.docstring:
Let $k(N)$ denote the smallest $k$ such that there exists
$N ≤ n_1 < ⋯ < n_k$ with $\frac 1 {n_1} + ... + \frac 1 {n_k} = 1$

Is it true that $\lim_{N \to \infty} k(N) - (e - 1)N = \infty$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/295](https://www.erdosproblems.com/295)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ Filter.Tendsto (fun N => ↑(Erdos295.k N) - (Real.exp 1 - 1) * ↑N) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop

declarations.docstring:
Erdős and Straus have proved the existence of some constant $c>0$
such that $-c < k(N)-(e-1)N \ll \frac N {\log N}$
references: [erdosproblems.com/295](https://www.erdosproblems.com/295)
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ C > 0,
  ∃ O > 0, ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ↑(Erdos295.k N) - (Real.exp 1 - 1) * ↑N ∈ Set.Ioc (-C) (O * ↑N / Real.log ↑N)

declarations.docstring:
Helper lemma: for each $N$, there exists $k$ and $n_1 < ... < n_k$ such that
$N ≤ n_1 < ⋯ < n_k$ with $\frac 1 {n_1} + ... + \frac 1 {n_k} = 1$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/295](https://www.erdosproblems.com/295)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (N : ℕ), ∃ k n, (∀ (i : Fin k.succ), N ≤ n i) ∧ StrictMono n ∧ ∑ i, 1 / ↑(n i) = 1

declarations.docstring:
Let $N\geq 1$ and let $k(N)$ be maximal such that there are $k$ disjoint $A_1,\ldots,A_k\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ with $\sum_{n\in A_i}\frac{1}{n}=1$ for all $i$. Estimate $k(N)$. Is it true that $k(N)=o(\log N)$?

Hunter and Sawhney observed that Bloom's theorem [Bl21], together with the greedy
argument, gives $k(N)=(1-o(1))\log N$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/296](https://www.erdosproblems.com/296)
[Bl21] Bloom, T. F., *On a density conjecture about unit fractions*. arXiv:2112.03726 (2021).
declarations.type_pretty:
(∀ (N k : ℕ), Erdos296.HasDisjointUnitDecomps N k → ↑k ≤ Erdos296.recipSum (Finset.Icc 1 N)) ∧
  ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → ε < 1 → ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, Erdos296.HasDisjointUnitDecomps N ⌊(1 - ε) * Real.log ↑N⌋₊

declarations.docstring:
Does every set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ of positive density contain some finite $S \subset A$ such that
$\sum_{n \in S} \frac{1}{n} = 1$?

The answer is yes, proved by Bloom [Bl21] (even if 'positive density' is interpreted as 'positive
upper density', which is likely what Erdős intended).

The theorem below uses the positive-upper-density interpretation; the literal natural-density
interpretation is recorded separately.

This was formalized in Lean 3 by Bloom and Mehta.
references: [erdosproblems.com/298](https://www.erdosproblems.com/298)
[Bl21] Bloom, T. F., On a density conjecture about unit fractions. arXiv:2112.03726 (2021).
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ (A : Set ℕ), 0 ∉ A → 0 < A.upperDensity → ∃ S, ↑S ⊆ A ∧ ∑ n ∈ S, 1 / ↑n = 1

declarations.docstring: The literal natural-density interpretation of Erdős Problem 298 follows from [Bl21].
references: [erdosproblems.com/298](https://www.erdosproblems.com/298)
[Bl21] Bloom, T. F., On a density conjecture about unit fractions. arXiv:2112.03726 (2021).
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ (A : Set ℕ), 0 ∉ A → A.HasPosDensity → ∃ S, ↑S ⊆ A ∧ ∑ n ∈ S, 1 / ↑n = 1

declarations.docstring:
Is there an infinite sequence $a_1 < a_2 < \dots$ such that $a_{i+1} - a_i = O(1)$ and no finite
sum of $\frac{1}{a_i}$ is equal to 1?

There does not exist such a sequence, which follows from the positive solution to
[erdosproblems.com/298] by Bloom [Bl21].

This was formalized in Lean 3 by Bloom and Mehta.
references: [erdosproblems.com/298](https://www.erdosproblems.com/298)
[erdosproblems.com/299](https://www.erdosproblems.com/299)
[Bl21] Bloom, T. F., On a density conjecture about unit fractions. arXiv:2112.03726 (2021).
declarations.type_pretty:
False ↔
  ∃ a,
    StrictMono a ∧
      (∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < a n) ∧
        (fun n => ↑(a (n + 1)) - ↑(a n)) =O[Filter.atTop] 1 ∧ ∀ (S : Finset ℕ), ∑ i ∈ S, 1 / ↑(a i) ≠ 1

declarations.docstring:
The corresponding question is also false if one replaces sequences such that $a_{i+1} - a_i = O(1)$
with sets of positive density, as follows from [Bl21].

The statement is as follows:
If $A \subset \mathbb{N}$ has positive upper density (and hence certainly if $A$ has positive
density) then there is a finite $S \subset A$ such that $\sum_{n \in S} \frac{1}{n} = 1$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/298](https://www.erdosproblems.com/298)
[erdosproblems.com/299](https://www.erdosproblems.com/299)
[Bl21] Bloom, T. F., On a density conjecture about unit fractions. arXiv:2112.03726 (2021).
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (A : Set ℕ), 0 ∉ A → 0 < A.upperDensity → ∃ S, ↑S ⊆ A ∧ ∑ n ∈ S, 1 / ↑n = 1

declarations.docstring:
If $A \subset \mathbb{N}$ has $\sum_{n \in A}\frac 1 n = \infty$, then must $A$ contain arbitrarily
long arithmetic progressions?
references: [erdosproblems.com/3](https://www.erdosproblems.com/3)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ (A : Set ℕ), (¬Summable fun a => 1 / ↑↑a) → ∃ᶠ (k : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ S ⊆ A, S.IsAPOfLength ↑k

declarations.docstring: Is it true that, for every $\varepsilon > 0$, $h(N) = \sqrt N + O_{\varepsilon}(N^\varepsilon)$
references: [erdosproblems.com/30](https://www.erdosproblems.com/30)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ ε > 0, (fun N => ↑(Erdos30.h N) - √↑N) =O[Filter.atTop] fun N => ↑N ^ ε

declarations.docstring:
Let $f(N)$ be the size of the largest $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ such that there are no
solutions to
$$\frac{1}{a}= \frac{1}{b}+\frac{1}{c}$$
with distinct $a,b,c\in A$? Estimate $f(N)$.

The colouring version of this is [303], which was solved by Brown and Rödl [BrRo91].
references: [erdosproblems.com/302](https://www.erdosproblems.com/302)
[BrRo91] Brown, Tom C. and Rödl, Voijtech, Monochromatic solutions to equations with unit fractions. Bull. Austral. Math. Soc. (1991), 387-392.
[ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
[va25](https://github.com/Woett/Mathematical-shorts/blob/main/Two-colouring%20and%20density%20lead%20to%20solutions%20to%20an%20equation%20in%20unit%20fractions.pdf)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (f : ℕ → ℕ),
  (∀ (N : ℕ), Erdos302.IsMaxNoTripleCard N (f N)) → Filter.Tendsto (fun N => ↑(f N) / ↑N) Filter.atTop (nhds sorry)

declarations.docstring:
In particular, is $f(N)=(\tfrac{1}{2}+o(1))N$?

This is false: it is contradicted by Cambie's lower bound of $(5/8+o(1))N$ recorded below,
since $5/8 > 1/2$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/302](https://www.erdosproblems.com/302)
[BrRo91] Brown, Tom C. and Rödl, Voijtech, Monochromatic solutions to equations with unit fractions. Bull. Austral. Math. Soc. (1991), 387-392.
[ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
[va25](https://github.com/Woett/Mathematical-shorts/blob/main/Two-colouring%20and%20density%20lead%20to%20solutions%20to%20an%20equation%20in%20unit%20fractions.pdf)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (f : ℕ → ℕ),
  (∀ (N : ℕ), Erdos302.IsMaxNoTripleCard N (f N)) → ¬Filter.Tendsto (fun N => ↑(f N) / ↑N) Filter.atTop (nhds (1 / 2))

declarations.docstring:
Stijn Cambie has observed that
$$f(N)\geq (5/8+o(1))N,$$
taking $A$ to be all odd integers $\leq N/4$ and all integers in $[N/2,N]$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/302](https://www.erdosproblems.com/302)
[BrRo91] Brown, Tom C. and Rödl, Voijtech, Monochromatic solutions to equations with unit fractions. Bull. Austral. Math. Soc. (1991), 387-392.
[ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
[va25](https://github.com/Woett/Mathematical-shorts/blob/main/Two-colouring%20and%20density%20lead%20to%20solutions%20to%20an%20equation%20in%20unit%20fractions.pdf)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (f : ℕ → ℕ),
  (∀ (N : ℕ), Erdos302.IsMaxNoTripleCard N (f N)) →
    ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, (5 / 8 - ε) * ↑N ≤ ↑(f N)

declarations.docstring:
One can take either $A$ to be all odd integers in $[1,N]$ or all integers in $[N/2,N]$ to show
$f(N)\geq (1/2+o(1))N$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/302](https://www.erdosproblems.com/302)
[BrRo91] Brown, Tom C. and Rödl, Voijtech, Monochromatic solutions to equations with unit fractions. Bull. Austral. Math. Soc. (1991), 387-392.
[ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
[va25](https://github.com/Woett/Mathematical-shorts/blob/main/Two-colouring%20and%20density%20lead%20to%20solutions%20to%20an%20equation%20in%20unit%20fractions.pdf)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (f : ℕ → ℕ),
  (∀ (N : ℕ), Erdos302.IsMaxNoTripleCard N (f N)) →
    ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, (1 / 2 - ε) * ↑N ≤ ↑(f N)

declarations.docstring:
Wouter van Doorn has proved [va25] that
$$f(N) \leq (9/10+o(1))N.$$
references: [erdosproblems.com/302](https://www.erdosproblems.com/302)
[BrRo91] Brown, Tom C. and Rödl, Voijtech, Monochromatic solutions to equations with unit fractions. Bull. Austral. Math. Soc. (1991), 387-392.
[ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
[va25](https://github.com/Woett/Mathematical-shorts/blob/main/Two-colouring%20and%20density%20lead%20to%20solutions%20to%20an%20equation%20in%20unit%20fractions.pdf)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (f : ℕ → ℕ),
  (∀ (N : ℕ), Erdos302.IsMaxNoTripleCard N (f N)) →
    ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ↑(f N) ≤ (9 / 10 + ε) * ↑N

declarations.docstring:
Is it true that in any finite colouring of the integers there exists a monochromatic solution
to $\frac 1 a = \frac 1 b + \frac 1 c$ with distinct $a, b, c$?

This is true, as proved by Brown and Rödl [BrRo91].

This was formalized in Lean by Yuan using Seed-Prover.
references: [erdosproblems.com/303](https://www.erdosproblems.com/303)
[BrRo91] Brown, Tom C. and Rödl, Voijtech, Monochromatic solutions to equations with unit fractions. Bull. Austral. Math. Soc. (1991), 387-392.
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (𝓒 : ℤ → ℤ),
    (Set.range 𝓒).Finite → ∃ a b c, [a, b, c, 0].Nodup ∧ 1 / ↑a = 1 / ↑b + 1 / ↑c ∧ (𝓒 '' {a, b, c}).Subsingleton

references: [erdosproblems.com/304](https://www.erdosproblems.com/304)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {a b : ℕ}, 1 ∈ Erdos304.unitFractionExpressible a b → a ∣ b

references: [erdosproblems.com/304](https://www.erdosproblems.com/304)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {a b : ℕ}, Erdos304.smallestCollection a b = 1 → a ∣ b

references: [erdosproblems.com/304](https://www.erdosproblems.com/304)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {a b : ℕ}, 1 ∈ Erdos304.unitFractionExpressible a b → ∃ m, 1 < m ∧ ↑a / ↑b = (↑m)⁻¹

references: [erdosproblems.com/304](https://www.erdosproblems.com/304)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {a b : ℕ}, Erdos304.smallestCollection a b = 1 → ∃ m, 1 < m ∧ ↑a / ↑b = (↑m)⁻¹

declarations.docstring:
Let $\frac a b\in \mathbb{Q}_{>0}$ with $b$ squarefree. Are there integers $1 < n_1 < \dots < n_k$,
each the product of two distinct primes, such that $\frac{a}{b}=\frac{1}{n_1}+\cdots+\frac{1}{n_k}$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/306](https://www.erdosproblems.com/306)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (q : ℚ),
    0 < q →
      Squarefree q.den →
        ∃ k n,
          n 0 = 1 ∧
            StrictMono n ∧
              (∀ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (Fin.last k),
                  ArithmeticFunction.cardDistinctFactors (n i) = 2 ∧ ArithmeticFunction.cardFactors (n i) = 2) ∧
                q = ∑ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (Fin.last k), 1 / ↑(n i)

declarations.docstring:
Every positive integer can be expressed as an Egyptian fraction where each denominator is the
product of three distinct primes.
references: [erdosproblems.com/306](https://www.erdosproblems.com/306)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (m : ℕ),
  0 < m →
    ∃ k > 0,
      ∃ n,
        n 0 = 1 ∧
          ∀ (i : ℕ) (hik : i < k),
            n ⟨i, ⋯⟩ < n ⟨i + 1, ⋯⟩ ∧
              (∀ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (Fin.last k),
                  ArithmeticFunction.cardDistinctFactors (n i) = 3 ∧ ArithmeticFunction.cardFactors (n i) = 3) ∧
                ↑m = ∑ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (Fin.last k), 1 / ↑(n i)

declarations.docstring:
Are there two finite set of primes $P$ and $Q$ such that

$$
1 = \left( \sum_{p \in P} \frac{1}{p} \right) \left( \sum_{q \in Q} \frac{1}{q} \right)
$$
?

Asked by Barbeau [Ba76].

[Ba76] Barbeau, E. J., _Computer challenge corner: Problem 477: A brute force program._
references: [erdosproblems.com/307](https://www.erdosproblems.com/307)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∃ P Q, (∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p) ∧ (∀ q ∈ Q, Nat.Prime q) ∧ 1 = (∑ p ∈ P, (↑p)⁻¹) * ∑ q ∈ Q, (↑q)⁻¹

declarations.docstring:
A machine-checked **barrier** for Erdős 307 (Bonfioli, 2026): any solution with `Q` nonempty uses at
least 59 primes in total, and `(∏_{p ∈ P} p)² ≥ 4·10¹¹²` — i.e. `∏_{p ∈ P} p ≥ 2·10⁵⁶` (and, by
symmetry, the same for `∏ Q`); so no solution lies below a prime-product of `2.09·10⁵⁶`. The full
`sorry`-free proof is in the linked repository (`Closed.lean`): the left conjunct is `card_ge_59`,
the right is `erdos307_barrier_closed`. Both depend on `propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound` and
nothing further: the evaluation of the first 59 primes is kernel-checked by `decide`, so no
`native_decide` enters this statement.
references: [erdosproblems.com/307](https://www.erdosproblems.com/307)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {P Q : Finset ℕ},
  (∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p) →
    (∀ q ∈ Q, Nat.Prime q) →
      Q.Nonempty → 1 = (∑ p ∈ P, (↑p)⁻¹) * ∑ q ∈ Q, (↑q)⁻¹ → 59 ≤ (P ∪ Q).card ∧ 4 * 10 ^ 112 ≤ (∏ p ∈ P, ↑p) ^ 2

declarations.docstring:
Instead of asking for sets of primes, ask only that all elements in the sets be relatively coprime.

Cambie has found several examples when this weakened version is true. For example,
$$
1=\left(1+\frac{1}{5}\right)\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3}\right)
$$
and
$$
1=\left(1+\frac{1}{41}\right)\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{7}\right).
$$
references: [erdosproblems.com/307](https://www.erdosproblems.com/307)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∃ P Q,
    0 ∉ P ∩ Q ∧
      1 < P.card ∧
        1 < Q.card ∧ (↑P).Pairwise Nat.Coprime ∧ (↑Q).Pairwise Nat.Coprime ∧ 1 = (∑ p ∈ P, (↑p)⁻¹) * ∑ q ∈ Q, (↑q)⁻¹

declarations.docstring: There are no examples known of the weakened coprime version if we insist that $1\not\in P\cup Q$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/307](https://www.erdosproblems.com/307)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∃ P Q,
    0 ∉ P ∩ Q ∧
      1 ∉ P ∪ Q ∧
        1 < P.card ∧
          1 < Q.card ∧ (↑P).Pairwise Nat.Coprime ∧ (↑Q).Pairwise Nat.Coprime ∧ 1 = (∑ p ∈ P, (↑p)⁻¹) * ∑ q ∈ Q, (↑q)⁻¹

declarations.docstring:
Given any infinite set $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ there is a set $B$ of density $0$ such that $A+B$ contains all except finitely many integers.

Conjectured by Erdős and Straus. Proved by Lorentz [Lo54].
references: [erdosproblems.com/31](https://www.erdosproblems.com/31)
[Er56] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in additive number theory*. Colloque sur la Théorie des Nombres, Bruxelles, 1955 (1956), 127-137.
[Er59] Erdős, P., *Über einige Probleme der additiven Zahlentheorie*. Sammelband zu Ehren des 250. Geburtstages Leonhard Eulers (1959), 116-119.
[Er65b] Erdős, Paul, *Some recent advances and current problems in number theory*. Lectures on Modern Mathematics, Vol. III (1965), 196-244.

[Er73](https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1973-21.pdf) Erdős, P., *Problems and results on combinatorial number theory*. A survey of combinatorial theory (Proc. Internat. Sympos., Colorado State Univ., Fort Collins, Colo., 1971) (1973), 117-138.
[Lo54] Lorentz, G. G., *On a problem of additive number theory*. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (1954), 838-841.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (A : Set ℕ), A.Infinite → ∃ B, B.HasDensity 0 ∧ ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, n ∈ A + B

declarations.docstring:
Does there exist a constant `c > 0` such that, for any `K > 1`, whenever `A` is a sufficiently large
finite multiset of integers with $\sum_{n \in A} 1/n > K$ there exists some $S \subseteq A$ such that
$1 - \exp(-(c*K)) < \sum_{n \in S} 1/n \le 1$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/312](https://www.erdosproblems.com/312)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∃ c,
    0 < c ∧
      ∀ (K : ℝ),
        1 < K →
          ∃ N₀,
            ∀ (n : ℕ) (a : Fin n → ℕ),
              n ≥ N₀ ∧ ∑ i, (↑(a i))⁻¹ > K →
                ∃ S, 1 - Real.exp (-(c * K)) < ∑ i ∈ S, (↑(a i))⁻¹ ∧ ∑ i ∈ S, (↑(a i))⁻¹ ≤ 1

declarations.docstring:
Let $n\geq 1$ and let $m$ be minimal such that $\sum_{n\leq k\leq m}\frac{1}{k}\geq 1$. We define
$$\epsilon(n) = \sum_{n\leq k\leq m}\frac{1}{k}-1.$$
How small can $\epsilon(n)$ be? Is it true that
$$\liminf n^2\epsilon(n)=0?$$

This is true, and shown by Lim and Steinerberger [LiSt24], who further proved that, for any
$\delta>0$, there exist infinitely many $n$ and $m$ such that
$$n^2\left\lvert \sum_{n\leq k\leq m}\frac{1}{k}-1\right\rvert\ll \frac{1}{(\log n)^{5/4-\delta}}.$$
Erdős and Graham (and also Lim and Steinerberger) believe that the exponent of $2$ is best
possible here, in that $\liminf \epsilon(n) n^{2+\delta}=\infty$ for all $\delta>0$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/314](https://www.erdosproblems.com/314)
[ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
[LiSt24] J. Lim and Steinerberger, S., *On differences of two harmonic numbers*. arXiv:2405.11354 (2024).
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ Filter.liminf (fun n => ↑n ^ 2 * Erdos314.epsilon n) Filter.atTop = 0

declarations.docstring:
Let $u_1=1$ and $u_{n+1}=u_n(u_n+1)$, so that $\sum_{k\geq 1}\frac{1}{u_k+1}$ and
$u_k=\lfloor c_0^{2^k}+1\rfloor$ for $k\geq 1$, where
$$c_0=\lim u_n^{1/2^n}=1.264085\cdots.$$
Let $a_1<a_2<\cdots $ be any other sequence with $\sum \frac{1}{a_k}=1$. Is it true that
$$\liminf a_n^{1/2^n}<c_0=1.264085\cdots?$$

This is true, and was proved independently by Kamio [Ka25] and Li and Tang [LiTa25].

An earlier interpretation of this question on this site defined $u_1=2$ and
$u_{n+1}=u_n^2-u_n+1$ (Sylvester's sequence), which is the same sequence shifted by $1$; we use
the phrasing above as more faithful to [ErGr80]. The constant $c_0$ is called the Vardi constant.
references: [erdosproblems.com/315](https://www.erdosproblems.com/315)
[ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
[Ka25] Y. Kamio, *Asymptotic analysis of infinite decompositions of a unit fraction into unit fractions*. arXiv:2503.02317 (2025).
[LiTa25] Z. Li and Q. Tang, *On a conjecture of Erdős and Graham about the Sylvester's sequence*. arXiv:2503.12277 (2025).
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ),
    (∀ (i : ℕ), 0 < a i) →
      StrictMono a →
        (∃ i, a i ≠ Erdos315.u i + 1) →
          ∑' (i : ℕ), 1 / ↑(a i) = 1 → Filter.liminf (fun i => ↑(a i) ^ (1 / 2) ^ (i + 1)) Filter.atTop < Erdos315.c₀

declarations.docstring:
Is it true that if $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}\setminus\{1\}$ is a finite set with
$\sum_{n \in A} \frac{1}{n} < 2$ then there is a partition $A=A_1 \sqcup A_2$
such that $\sum_{n \in A_i} \frac{1}{n} < 1$ for $i=1,2$?

This is not true in general, as shown by Sándor [Sa97].

The minimal counterexample is $\{2,3,4,5,6,7,10,11,13,14,15\}$, found by Tom Stobart.

This was formalized in Lean by Mehta.
references: [erdosproblems.com/316](https://www.erdosproblems.com/316)
[Sa97] Sándor, Csaba, On a problem of Erdős. J. Number Theory (1997), 203-210.
declarations.type_pretty:
False ↔
  ∀ (A : Finset ℕ),
    0 ∉ A →
      1 ∉ A → ∑ n ∈ A, 1 / ↑n < 2 → ∃ A₁ A₂, Disjoint A₁ A₂ ∧ A = A₁ ∪ A₂ ∧ ∑ n ∈ A₁, 1 / ↑n < 1 ∧ ∑ n ∈ A₂, 1 / ↑n < 1

declarations.docstring:
This is not true in general, as shown by Sándor [Sa97], who observed that the proper divisors of
$120$ form a counterexample. More generally, Sándor shows that for any $n\geq 2$ there exists a
finite set $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}\backslash\{1\}$ with $\sum_{k\in A}\frac{1}{k} < n$ and no
partition into $n$ parts each of which has $\sum_{k\in A_i}\frac{1}{k}<1$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/316](https://www.erdosproblems.com/316)
[Sa97] Sándor, Csaba, On a problem of Erdős. J. Number Theory (1997), 203-210.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (n : ℕ),
  2 ≤ n →
    ∃ A,
      A.Nonempty ∧
        0 ∉ A ∧
          1 ∉ A ∧ ∑ k ∈ A, 1 / ↑k < ↑n ∧ ∀ (P : Finpartition A), P.parts.card = n → ∃ p ∈ P.parts, 1 ≤ ∑ n ∈ p, 1 / ↑n

declarations.docstring: This is not true if $A$ is a multiset, for example $2,3,3,5,5,5,5$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/316](https://www.erdosproblems.com/316)
[Sa97] Sándor, Csaba, On a problem of Erdős. J. Number Theory (1997), 203-210.
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ A,
  0 ∉ A ∧
    1 ∉ A ∧
      (Multiset.map (fun x => 1 / x) do
              let a ← A
              pure ↑a).sum <
          2 ∧
        ∀ (A₁ A₂ : Multiset ℕ),
          A = A₁ + A₂ →
            1 ≤
                (Multiset.map (fun x => 1 / x) do
                    let a ← A₁
                    pure ↑a).sum ∨
              1 ≤
                (Multiset.map (fun x => 1 / x) do
                    let a ← A₂
                    pure ↑a).sum

declarations.docstring:
There exists a set `A` with positive density that does not have property `P₁`.
#TODO: prove this lemma by assuming `erdos_318.contain_single_even`.

The density sits in an existential, so `HasPosDensity` is the *stronger* reading here and
weakening it to positive lower density would claim less, which is the opposite of the usual
situation for Erdős' "positive density". It also costs nothing: by
`erdos_318.variants.contain_single_even` a witness only needs exactly one even element, and the
odd numbers together with one even number have density `1 / 2` on the nose.

Acta Arith. (2001), 99-114.

declarations.docstring:
